title: Calendar parts and truncations agree with the reference from 0001 to 9999
verdict: native in 0001-01-01 … 9999-12-31 on TIMESTAMP (µs); the written plan raises outside
description: At 0001-01-01, the leap days 0004-02-29, 1600-02-29 and 2000-02-29, 1900-02-28 and 1900-03-01 (1900 is not a leap year), both sides of the Gregorian switch (1582-10-04 and 1582-10-15, ten days apart in history and eleven in the proleptic calendar) and 9999-12-31, each at 23:59:59.999999, the engine gives the proleptic Gregorian values `core/Sverify/Core/Time.lean`'s `#guard`s give: 0001-01-01 is a Monday (its own week), the week of 9999-12-31 starts 9999-12-27, its ISO week is 52 and its weekday Friday.

sverify writes timestamps as DuckDB's `TIMESTAMP`, microseconds since 1970 (`sql/duckdb.py`), which reaches beyond 0001 … 9999 (to 294247 AD, duckdb-date-range); `TIMESTAMP_NS` would cover only 1677 … 2262.
reference: D32: the reference's timestamps are 0001-01-01 00:00:00 to 9999-12-31 23:59:59.999999 (`Time.tsMin`, `Time.tsMax`); `date_part`, truncation to a week or longer, `date_bin`, `strftime` and adding months raise outside them (`Issue.overflow`), and the writers guard, since the engine computes there.

provenance.checked_by: D32 probe (session youthful-margulis), duckdb 2.0.0, macOS arm64
